title: POC scoping: MediWell - Quality Eval Plan
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan: define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, workload sizing and benchmark timelines. Agreement to run an initial 2-week golden prompt regression, with a 4-week POC including automated scoring and live latency/cost benchmarks. Action items: Redwood to share eval template and benchmark script; MediWell to provide 200 golden prompts + 2k held-out cases and success criteria. Security questions around SSO/KMS and data retention to be answered in follow-up.
next_steps: Redwood to share Quality Eval template and scoring rubric (link) by 2025-07-23
MediWell to share initial set of 200 golden prompts and 2k held-out test cases by 2025-07-28
Schedule 30-min benchmark run kickoff week of 2025-07-28
Security follow-up to answer SSO/KMS/data retention questions by 2025-07-24

transcript:
Meeting header:
2025-07-21 15:00 UTC - Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Nina Roberts (Head of ML, MediWell), Juan Garcia (Product), Leah Kim (Security), Priya Singh (Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be noisy): Discussed POC scope and quality eval plan; agreed on deliverables and timeline; security follow-up requested.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call — Alex here from Redwood, Samir is our SE and Dana's going to help run the POC.
00:12 Nina Roberts: Hi thanks, Nina here. We wanted to focus this call on the quality evaluation plan and how we measure regressions and hallucinations during the POC.
00:20 Alex Chen: Perfect. Goal for today is to lock success criteria, dataset sizes, what counts as a regression, and the scoring approach. Samir, want to take the tech side?
00:29 Samir Patel: Sure. Quick note on infra: we'll run the benchmarks on Redwood Hosted and a Dedicated configuration for parity — we suggest starting against Redwood Hosted / latest open checkpoint then run a Dedicated run with the same model variant. We'll capture latency, p95, cost/token. Also we'll run the quality eval offline using our eval harness.
00:52 Juan Garcia: Quick question — for "quality eval harness", is that the same script you used in the demo last month, or is there a standard rubric?
01:01 Samir Patel: It's the same harness but we have a configurable rubric. It supports unit checks: format validation, hallucination detectors, and embedding-similarity scoring. We can expose thresholds.
01:15 Leah Kim: To scope security, can you confirm data residency and retention for the POC? We need to know whether prompts or model outputs are stored and for how long.
01:24 Alex Chen: Yes — for Hosted POC we can set a short retention window and mask tokens on ingest; for Dedicated/Private deployments data stays within your VPC. We'll share the retention defaults and options.
01:36 Nina Roberts: Great. On the quality plan — our core success metric is "regression <= 2%" across golden prompts on answer correctness and format. We also care about hallucination rate: target < 1% hallucination on diagnosis prompts.
01:52 Samir Patel: Helpful to be explicit: define the golden prompt set (we recommend ~200 high-value prompts), a held-out validation of, say, 2k cases for statistical significance, and a small fuzz set for edge cases. For scoring we typically use a hybrid approach: 1) format checks (binary pass/fail), 2) semantic similarity via embedding cosine (thresholded), 3) token-level metrics for structured outputs (exact match / normalized edit distance).
02:20 Priya Singh: For embedding thresholds, do you have a baseline we can use — e.g., cosine > 0.85 is considered matching?
02:27 Samir Patel: Yes, for short clinical answers we usually start at 0.82–0.88. We'll calibrate on your golden set. Also we include human-in-the-loop checks for any items that fall in the gray zone (0.78–0.82).
02:45 Juan Garcia: On hallucination detection — how automated is that? We can't have nurses reading thousands of outputs.
02:52 Samir Patel: We run a combination: rule-based checks for unsupported assertions (e.g., stating a patient has a condition not in the prompt), citation checks if you require references, and an LLM-based hallucination classifier trained on clinical pairs. It's not perfect, but it triages candidates for human review.
03:10 Nina Roberts: That classifier — is it open-source or proprietary? And how often are false positives/negatives?
03:18 Samir Patel: It's a Redwood internal classifier, tuned on healthcare pairs; we typically see 85–92% precision at thresholds tuned for recall as desired. We'll surface ROC metrics in the eval report.
03:34 Leah Kim: Important: we need to ensure PII is never logged. For Hosted runs, can you ensure PII masking on ingest and that logs are disabled or stored encrypted? Also SSO/SAML for access to the console.
03:49 Alex Chen: Absolutely. We'll share our SOC2 artifacts, SAML config doc, and our KMS options. For the POC we can enable token redaction and set logs to 7-day retention. For Dedicated you control KMS keys.
04:04 Juan Garcia: Back to success criteria — Nina mentioned regression <= 2% on golden prompts. Do we put a pass/fail gating for deployment?
04:12 Nina Roberts: We want gating for model rollout in production. If regression exceeds 2% or hallucination > 1% we'd require a rollback or manual review. During POC we want to compare new model variants to our baseline (current in-house model).
04:27 Samir Patel: We'll run paired A/B tests and can compute bootstrap confidence intervals on the delta. We'll export per-prompt differences so you can see which prompts regress.
04:38 Juan Garcia: Timeline question: how long to run the initial eval?
04:42 Alex Chen: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) — alignment and data share; Week 1 — ingest golden prompts and run initial calibration; Week 2 — run the automated regression suite across 2k holdout cases and produce a benchmark report; Weeks 3–4 — optional Dedicated run and any tuning. So a 4-week POC with a 2-week fast fail window.
05:05 Priya Singh: For workload sizing, what throughput should we test against? Our expected QPS is 8 requests/sec at 1k average tokens, with peaks to 30 QPS.
05:15 Samir Patel: For bench sizing we'll simulate your distribution: avg seq len 1k tokens, 8 sustained QPS, 30 QPS spike. We'll measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and cost/token. We'll also test batching and KV cache benefits for repeated prefixes — e.g., discharge summary templates.
05:37 Nina Roberts: On caching — does your runtime support prefix KV cache across users? We need per-tenant isolation but want cache wins.
05:45 Samir Patel: Yes, we support isolated KV caches per tenant and can do shared cold-start caches for similar prompts. There was a note in earlier demos where "K V cash" got misread — yeah, K V cache.
05:56 Alex Chen: (laughs) transcripts love to mangle that.
06:00 Juan Garcia: For the quality eval outputs, can you provide the raw outputs plus the scored metrics? We want to feed them into our dashboard and have per-prompt traceability.
06:09 Samir Patel: We export JSONL with original prompt, model output, score vectors (format_pass, embedding_score, hallucination_flag, normalized_edit_distance), and human labels where available. We'll also include a CSV summary.
06:26 Leah Kim: Those exports — where do they land? S3 bucket under our account?
06:31 Alex Chen: For Hosted POC we can ship to a pre-authorized S3 or to Redwood's secure transfer; for Dedicated we can write directly to your bucket inside the VPC. We'll include kms:key-id guidance.
06:45 Nina Roberts: Let's talk about golden prompts. We plan to send 200 gold prompts spanning triage, diagnosis suggestion, and discharge formatting. Any recommendations for coverage?
06:55 Samir Patel: Good split: 40% structured template outputs (discharge, billing codes), 40% short-answer clinical Qs, 20% long-form reasoning. Include negative cases where the model should abstain. Also include edge cases and hallucination traps (ambiguous dates, contrived meds).
07:15 Priya Singh: We'll annotate golden prompts with expected outputs and tolerance — e.g., exact match for templates, similarity threshold for narrative.
07:23 Alex Chen: Perfect. We'll provide a sample annotation schema and a CSV template.
07:27 Juan Garcia: On regression tests, do you run them automatically on new model pushes?
07:31 Samir Patel: During the POC we can schedule nightly runs against new model variants; in production we recommend gating via CI/CD integration that flags regressions and can block rollout.
07:42 Nina Roberts: For hallucination checks, can we get per-prompt explanation why flagged? Our clinicians want context when something is marked.
07:49 Samir Patel: We'll include an explanation blob — rule hits + classifier probability + nearest evidence from prompt (if citation available). Where the classifier triggers, we'll attach top-k supporting tokens that triggered the rule.
08:05 Juan Garcia: Scoring approach summary — can you lay out the numeric rubric we'll use?
08:10 Samir Patel: Sure. Composite score (0–100): 40 points format/structure (binary pass with weighted penalties), 40 points semantic correctness (embedding similarity scaled to 0–40), 10 points hallucination penalty (subtracted if flagged), 10 points fluency/readability (BLEU/ROUGE proxy normalized). We'll provide thresholds — pass >= 85 for golden prompts, and regression defined as drop > 2 points absolute average across the golden set.
08:38 Nina Roberts: Is BLEU reliable for our content? For long-form reasoning it might be noisy.
08:43 Samir Patel: Agreed — BLEU is weaker for long-form. That's why we weight semantic embedding more for narratives, and exact-match for structured outputs. We'll tune per-prompt type.
08:57 Leah Kim: A note on audit logs — we need an immutable audit trail for scored results for regulatory purposes. Is that available?
09:04 Alex Chen: Yes — we can export audit trails with hashing and timestamping; for Dedicated you can plug your SIEM. We'll include a sample audit output in the eval report.
09:18 Dana Ortiz: Quick check on deliverables: Alex, share eval template and sample outputs; Samir, provide benchmark config; Priya, deliver prompts. Is that right?
09:26 Alex Chen: Yep. Also call out that for the initial 2-week run we'll focus on the golden 200 + 2k holdout to validate thresholds. If we hit pass gating, we'll expand to full traffic simulation.
09:38 Juan Garcia: If we fail gating, what's the remediation path? Roll back to baseline and open an RFC?
09:44 Samir Patel: Correct — automatic rollback policy or manual hold and remediation. We'll document the steps in the playbook.
09:52 Nina Roberts: Can we see an example report? The demo had one but it'd help to see the actual eval CSV and JSONL schema.
09:58 Alex Chen: We'll share the exact report and a mock filled with synthetic results. Link will be in the follow-up.
10:05 Leah Kim: For SSO, do you support Okta SAML? Also SCIM for provisioning?
10:09 Alex Chen: Yes to Okta SAML and SCIM for provisioning users; we'll include the metadata files.
10:15 Priya Singh: Anything else on data labeling? We may add a small human review panel for borderline items — can Redwood provide an interface?
10:23 Samir Patel: We have a lightweight review UI for adjudication that you can use during the POC; it supports batch labeling and marking root causes. We'll enable access for a few reviewer accounts.
10:34 Nina Roberts: That helps. Timeline recap?
10:36 Alex Chen: Recap: Redwood deliver by 7/23: eval template, benchmark scripts, sample report. MediWell deliver by 7/28: 200 gold prompts + 2k holdout. Kickoff benchmark week of 7/28 with initial report by end of week 8/1. Security docs by 7/24. POC ends week of 8/18 unless extended.
10:58 Juan Garcia: Sounds good. Anything else?
11:02 Leah Kim: One ask — include data deletion steps in the docs explicitly.
11:06 Alex Chen: Will do.
11:10 Dana Ortiz: I'll send calendar invites for the benchmark runs and set up the shared drive.
11:14 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and action items.
11:19 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription quality: some mis-hearings present (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache, Redwood product names sometimes truncated).
